interpretation_specific_to_normative_mod.reason: The discussion section provides a thorough interpretation of the results in the context of normative modeling. It explicitly highlights the advantages over traditional case-control GLM analyses by showing it can detect differences (between PD risk groups) that GLM misses. It discusses the clinical prospects and meaning of the 'total outlier count' as a personalized measure.
interpretation_specific_to_normative_mod.supporting_text: Importantly, conventional GLM group-average analyses did not reveal atrophy differences between these groups. Total outlier count is agnostic to the regional location of cortical atrophy, whereas conventional GLM approaches require cortical atrophy to be in the same locations between individuals.

additional_comments.additional_comments: A major strength of this study is its use of a large, pre-existing normative model and its application to clinically well-defined patient groups, including a novel stratification of PD patients by dementia risk. The direct comparison with conventional GLM analysis, which fails to find a difference that the normative modeling approach successfully identifies, provides a compelling demonstration of the method's value in heterogeneous diseases. The handling of potential outliers in the primary outcome measure through sensitivity analysis is also a mark of high-quality research.
